title: Shampoo – do we really need to use it
titleChinese: 我们真的需要用洗发水吗？
paragraphs: Buying shampoo can be overwhelming – there are so many brands to choose from, across a huge range of prices. Some brands promise to repair and nourish our hair, while others promise to strengthen and add volume. But are any of these claims true? Do we even need shampoo at all?

Since long before shampoo was invented – some say in India – our bodies have been producing sebum – an oil-like substance. Sebum stops our skin from getting dry, manages the health of our scalp and makes our hair shiny. But it also collects dirt, and, if left untouched for too long, sebum can cause our hair to become greasy. There are no disadvantages from a health perspective to letting our hair be greasy, says Eleanore Richardson, Trichologist at Fulham Scalp and Hair Clinic, but many people choose to wash their hair regularly for aesthetic reasons.

And so we reach for the shampoo bottle. Shampoos contain a group of chemicals called surfactants. They grab the dirt and grease from the surface of our hair, meaning when we rinse away the shampoo, we also wash away the grease and dirt. But, as Laura Waters, who's a Professor of Pharmaceutical Analysis in the School of Applied Sciences at Huddersfield University, points out, 'some surfactants work too well' and take the natural oils out of the hair, as well. More expensive shampoos may contain less harsh surfactants, but – adds Laura Waters – the type of shampoo doesn't really matter. 'It's on our hair very briefly and gets washed away'. It's the conditioners and styling products that we use after the shampoo that make a bigger difference to the texture and feel of our hair.

Of course, the more we put onto our hair, the more we need to cleanse it off, creating a vicious circle. So, yes, it seems we do have a need for shampoo, but we also shouldn't expect it to be a miracle cure. And, finally, next time you're in a shampoo aisle, remember that hair is made up of dead protein cells and that, sadly, not even the most expensive shampoo can bring them back to life.

vocabulary.translation: 这款面霜滋养干燥的肌肤。

vocabulary.translation: 这款摩丝能让细软头发更蓬松。

sentences.english: Buying shampoo can be overwhelming – there are so many brands to choose from, across a huge range of prices.

sentences.chinese: 一些品牌承诺可以修护、滋养头发，另一些则声称可以强韧发丝、增加发量。

sentences.english: But are any of these claims true?
sentences.chinese: 但这些说法究竟属实吗？

sentences.english: Do we even need shampoo at all?
sentences.chinese: 我们真的需要洗发水吗？

sentences.chinese: 早在洗发水被发明之前（有人称其起源于印度），我们的身体就一直在分泌皮脂——一种油脂状物质。

sentences.english: Sebum stops our skin from getting dry, manages the health of our scalp and makes our hair shiny.
sentences.chinese: 皮脂能防止皮肤干燥，维持头皮健康，让头发富有光泽。

sentences.english: But it also collects dirt, and, if left untouched for too long, sebum can cause our hair to become greasy.
sentences.chinese: 但它也会吸附污垢，若长时间不清理，皮脂会让头发变得油腻。

sentences.english: There are no disadvantages from a health perspective to letting our hair be greasy, says Eleanore Richardson, Trichologist at Fulham Scalp and Hair Clinic, but many people choose to wash their hair regularly for aesthetic reasons.
sentences.chinese: 富勒姆头皮与头发诊所的毛发学家埃莉诺·理查森表示，从健康角度来看，头发油腻并无坏处，但许多人出于美观原因会选择定期洗头。

sentences.english: And so we reach for the shampoo bottle.
sentences.chinese: 于是我们便拿起了洗发水瓶。

sentences.english: Shampoos contain a group of chemicals called surfactants. They grab the dirt and grease from the surface of our hair, meaning when we rinse away the shampoo, we also wash away the grease and dirt.
sentences.chinese: 洗发水含有一类名为表面活性剂的化学物质，它们会吸附头发表面的污垢和油脂，这意味着冲洗洗发水时，我们也一并洗掉了油脂和污垢。

sentences.english: But, as Laura Waters, who's a Professor of Pharmaceutical Analysis in the School of Applied Sciences at Huddersfield University, points out, 'some surfactants work too well' and take the natural oils out of the hair, as well.
sentences.chinese: 但哈德斯菲尔德大学应用科学学院药物分析教授劳拉·沃特斯指出，“有些表面活性剂效果过强”，还会带走头发中的天然油脂。

sentences.english: More expensive shampoos may contain less harsh surfactants, but – adds Laura Waters – the type of shampoo doesn't really matter.
sentences.chinese: 更昂贵的洗发水可能含有刺激性较小的表面活性剂，但劳拉·沃特斯补充道，什么样的洗发水其实无关紧要。

sentences.english: 'It's on our hair very briefly and gets washed away'.
sentences.chinese: “它在头发上停留的时间极短，很快就被冲洗掉了。”

sentences.english: It's the conditioners and styling products that we use after the shampoo that make a bigger difference to the texture and feel of our hair.
sentences.chinese: 真正对头发的质感和触感影响更大的，是洗发后使用的护发素和造型产品。

sentences.english: Of course, the more we put onto our hair, the more we need to cleanse it off, creating a vicious circle.
sentences.chinese: 当然，我们往头发上涂抹的产品越多，就越需要将其清洗干净，这就形成了一个恶性循环。

sentences.english: So, yes, it seems we do have a need for shampoo, but we also shouldn't expect it to be a miracle cure.
sentences.chinese: 所以，我们确实需要洗发水，但也不该指望它是万能灵药。

sentences.english: And, finally, next time you're in a shampoo aisle, remember that hair is made up of dead protein cells and that, sadly, not even the most expensive shampoo can bring them back to life.
sentences.chinese: 最后，下次你身处洗发水货架区时，要记住头发由死亡的蛋白质细胞构成，遗憾的是，即便最昂贵的洗发水也无法让它们重获生机。
